subject: Maths
title: Enlargement
subtitle: Transformations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can enlarge a shape by a given scale factor from a centre of enlargement.

key_vocab.definition: An enlargement changes the size of a shape by a scale factor from a fixed point called the centre of enlargement.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can enlarge a shape by a given scale factor from a centre of enlargement.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: enlargement -- An enlargement changes the size of a shape by a scale factor from a fixed point called the centre of enlargement.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply the distance from the centre to each vertex by the scale factor to find the image vertices.
image distance = SF × object distance from centre
Measure distances from the centre of enlargement

Key examples:
  ✓ SF 2 from centre: all distances from centre doubled  (shape is twice as big)
  ✓ SF &frac{1}{2}: image is half the size  (reduction)
  ✓ SF -1: image inverted through the centre  (rotated 180°)
  ✗ Enlargement changes angles  (angles stay the same)
  ✗ SF 3 triples the area  (area scales by SF² = 9)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – scale factor 2 from origin
  Enlarge triangle (1,1), (3,1), (1,3) by SF 2 from (0,0).
  Multiply each coordinate by 2
  (1,1)→(2,2), (3,1)→(6,2), (1,3)→(2,6)
  Image is twice the size
  (2,2), (6,2), (2,6)
  (From the origin, just multiply all coordinates by the SF.)

Example 2 – scale factor 3 from a point
  Enlarge point (2,1) by SF 3 from centre (1,0).
  Vector from centre to point: (2-1, 1-0) = (1, 1)
  Multiply by 3: (3, 3)
  Image = centre + (3,3) = (4, 3)
  (4, 3)
  (Find the vector from centre to point, multiply by SF, add back to centre.)

sections.title: SF 2 from origin
sections.content:
Enlarge each point by SF 2 from (0,0).

(a) (1, 2)
(b) (3, 1)
(c) (2, 4)
(d) (0, 3)

sections.title: SF 3 from origin
sections.content:
Enlarge each point by SF 3 from (0,0).

(a) (1, 1)
(b) (2, 0)
(c) (1, 3)
(d) (4, 2)

sections.title: From a non-origin centre
sections.content:
Enlarge by SF 2 from the given centre.

(a) Point (3,2), centre (1,1)
(b) Point (4,3), centre (2,1)
(c) Point (5,1), centre (3,1)
(d) Point (1,4), centre (0,2)

sections.title: Fractional scale factors
Mixed enlargement
sections.content:
Perform each enlargement.

(a) (2,3) SF 2 from (0,0)
(b) (4,1) SF 3 from (1,0)
(c) (6,8) SF &frac{1}{2} from (0,0)
(d) (3,2) SF -1 from (2,2)
(e) (5,1) SF -2 from (3,1)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ An enlargement with SF 2 doubles all lengths
✗ Enlargement with SF 2 doubles the area
✓ Angles remain the same after enlargement
✗ A negative scale factor puts the image on the same side
✓ SF between 0 and 1 makes the shape smaller
